end.summary:
Manav identified foods eaten by common animals, including animals that eat both seeds and insects.
They built and read food chains using arrows in two examples.
They observed that a plant in sunlight makes food, while one kept in darkness does not.
They predicted population and food changes when snakes, owls, or bees are removed.
They did not yet explain that plants make their own food and start every food chain.
end.parentNote: Asha practised plant-eaters, meat-eaters, animals that eat both, food-chain arrows, and what can happen when one part is removed. Manav used the chain relationships to reason that removing snakes or owls can increase mice and reduce grain, and that fewer bees can mean fewer fruits and vegetables. They mixed up the role of plants and soil, and this was not corrected in the lesson. At home, ask Manav to draw one food chain and circle the plant that starts it.
